title: Google & MongoDB launch AI agent integration
summary: Google and MongoDB partner to launch native AI agent database integration
detailed: Google and MongoDB have introduced a MongoDB integration for Google's Agent Development Kit, adding session storage, memory and retrieval features for AI agents.
The new integration centres on ADK 2.0, which Google describes as the orchestration layer for multi-agent systems, with MongoDB providing storage for sessions and memory.
The software can be installed through the Python package manager using the google-adk[mongodb] package, adding MongoDB support directly into ADK development environments.
The integration supports MongoDB Atlas and self-managed MongoDB 8.0+ deployments for vector and hybrid search.
sentences: Google and MongoDB have introduced a MongoDB integration for Google's Agent Development Kit, adding session storage, memory and retrieval features for AI agents.
The software connects MongoDB with Google's open-source ADK framework, which is used to build, debug and deploy AI agents.
It is designed to let developers store agent sessions and longer-term memory in MongoDB, while using MongoDB Search to retrieve operational data.
Google's ADK is available in Python, TypeScript, Go, Java and Kotlin.
The new integration centres on ADK 2.0, which Google describes as the orchestration layer for multi-agent systems, with MongoDB providing storage for sessions and memory.
According to the companies, the aim is to give developers a single data layer for application data, agent state and retrieval tasks.
This is intended to reduce the need for separate databases or synchronisation pipelines when moving an AI agent from prototype to production.
A key part of the release is the MongoDbSessionService class, which stores sessions, events, and application, user and session state in MongoDB.
It includes optimistic concurrency control to help applications manage concurrent updates safely, along with configurable collections to fit existing data architectures.
The integration also includes a MongoDbMemoryService class for agents that need memory beyond a single session.
It ingests session events into MongoDB collections and retrieves relevant memories through keyword matching.
MongoDB says memory ingestion is idempotent, helping to avoid duplication if an application adds the same session more than once.
Developers can use the service to add a session to memory and search stored memory for relevant information tied to a user or application.
The release also adds MongoDbToolset support for AI agents that need access to product catalogues, documents or other operational records already stored in MongoDB.
This lets agents call search tools within ADK while the application retains control of the database connection, configuration and index settings.
According to the companies, the search component supports semantic and hybrid retrieval.
In practice, this means developers can build agents for tasks such as product discovery, knowledge assistance, support workflows and specialised copilots using the same database layer.
Support covers MongoDB Atlas as well as self-managed MongoDB 8.0 and newer deployments for vector and hybrid search.
Developers can connect through a connection string or use an existing PyMongo client, and can configure index names, embedding fields, result limits and candidate counts through MongoDbToolSettings.

The integration reflects a broader shift in the AI software market as companies try to move agents from demonstrations into operational systems that can preserve user context across multiple interactions.
In that environment, session persistence and memory have become central design questions alongside model choice.
Google says ADK supplies the framework and tool interface, while the MongoDB integration provides the persistence layer beneath it.
The setup is intended to support agents that maintain conversation history independently of a single machine and carry a user's history across sessions.
The underlying ADK platform integrates with Gemini models, including Gemini 4 Argon for multi-step reasoning and Gemini 3.8 Flash for lower-latency execution.
The companies say ADK 2.0 also provides standardised tool-calling interfaces, native telemetry and access controls.
The software can be installed through the Python package manager using the google-adk[mongodb] package, adding MongoDB support directly into ADK development environments.
The integration supports MongoDB Atlas and self-managed MongoDB 8.0+ deployments for vector and hybrid search.
